description: Conflicting evidence on a high-impact transaction. One communication looks like invoice fraud; another is a plausible legitimate explanation from the same counterparty. Risk lands mid-band and confidence is genuinely low - the system does not know, and says so.

customer.normal_activity: Business account. Regular supplier payments, occasional bank-detail updates.

signals.redacted_quote: our account details have changed, please use the new ones

evidence.claim: Supplier emailed new bank details shortly before the payment - the signature pattern of invoice-redirection fraud
evidence.redacted_quote: our account details have changed, please use the new ones

evidence.claim: A later call from a number matching the supplier's registered landline confirms a genuine banking migration, which contradicts the fraud reading
Beneficiary name is unchanged and the amount matches an outstanding invoice, but the account number changed 100 minutes before payment

demo_note: This scenario exposed a missing rule. Risk is 58 - mid-band - so the original gate returned HOLD, which means an analyst could have released a 30000 USD payment without anyone weighing the contradiction. rule.high_impact_low_confidence was added because of this case: confidence 0.44 on a high-impact transaction goes to a named human, regardless of what risk says. This is the thesis working - uncertainty reduced autonomy, and the reason the AI stepped back was that it did not know, not that the number was high.
